answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when its messages are proven to violate a consensus rule, such as double-signing the same task result. A sybil attacker must lock capital in every fake account, while honest agents recover their stake; creating identities is cheap, but keeping a spiral of them active becomes costly as each must risk funds. A public cipher can bind each stake to one signing key, and a pigment-like marker in the ledger can make repeated slashing visible to evaluators.
